**Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is generally fine on a flight, as long as it's in your carry-on.**

**Why it works**
- The FAA limit for spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks is 100 Wh per battery. The FAA also says power banks are allowed in carry-on only, never in checked bags ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- To check your own bank, divide mAh by 1000 to get Ah, then multiply by the voltage. A typical 20,000 mAh bank runs at about 3.7 V, so 20 Ah × 3.7 V ≈ 74 Wh. That is well under 100 Wh.
- The Wh rating is often printed on the battery. If it is, use that number.

**Rules to follow**
- **Carry-on only.** If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Use the original packaging, tape over the ports, a pouch, or a case to prevent short circuits.
- **Don't bring a damaged or recalled one.** The FAA prohibits these in any bag.
- **Check your airline's policy.** Many airlines set stricter limits, including a cap on how many power banks you can carry, whatever their capacity. The FAA says to check with your carrier before you travel.
- **Tell the crew right away** if the bank gets hot, swells, or smokes during the flight.
